The trip

Brazil Southernlands

Brazil is one of the world's great surf nations — home to world champions, 8,000 kilometers of coastline, and a surf culture that runs deep. Yet international surf tourism there is almost nonexistent.

Brazil Southernlands takes you to Santa Catarina, in the south. Consistent waves, real surf culture, and a place most international surfers will never find on their own.

This is not a surf holiday. It is a structured coaching program in one of Brazil's most underrated coastal regions, with a maximum of four surfers per trip.

LocationImbituba, Santa Catarina
Duration10 nights
Group sizeMaximum 4 surfers
Coaching20+ hours in-water & video analysis
LevelIntermediate to advanced
What's included
Your surf coaching — in the water and on screen
Every session is coached from the water and recorded on video. After each surf we sit down together, review the footage, and build a clear picture of what to work on next. 20+ hours across 10 days — enough time to make real changes to how you surf.
Daily surf sessions at curated breaks
We surf the best breaks in the region based on conditions each day. Small group, no crowds, no wasted time.
Private house accommodation
The group stays together in a private house in Imbituba. Comfortable, well-located, and exclusively yours for the 10 nights.
Daily breakfast & lunch
Fresh, local food to fuel your sessions. Breakfast and lunch are taken care of every day of the trip.
Daily yoga sessions
A daily yoga session with a local instructor, focused on surf-specific mobility and recovery.
Hiking trip for sightseeing
A full day out exploring the region — one of the most scenic and underrated landscapes in southern Brazil.
All photo & video footage
All footage from your surf sessions is yours to keep. You leave with a full record of your progression.
Airport transfers & ground transport
We handle all transfers to and from Florianópolis airport, and all transport during the trip.
What's not included

Flights to Brazil. Dinners (except the private chef night). Lunch and dinner on the hiking day. Surf equipment — surfboards, leashes, and wetsuits. Intermediate to advanced surfers are expected to bring their own gear. We are happy to help you find or source equipment if needed.

How the days unfold

10 nights in the
south of Brazil

Day 1
Arrival
Transfer from airport. Settle into the house. Welcome dinner with the chef. Group briefing and surfer evaluation.
Days 2 – 5
Coaching intensive
Morning surf with in-water coaching. Afternoon video analysis and technical debrief. Free surf when conditions are on.
Day 6
Yoga & rest
Morning yoga with a local instructor. Afternoon free surf or rest. A recovery day built into the rhythm.
Day 7
Serra do Tabuleiro
A full day off the water. Hiking through Serra do Tabuleiro with a local guide. New perspective, active recovery.
Days 8 – 10
Final sessions
Back in the water with fresh legs. More coaching hours, free surf, and a closing dinner with the chef.
Day 11
Departure
Final morning surf if conditions allow. Transfer to airport.
About Lin

Coached from
lived experience

I started surfing young and competed at international level, representing Argentina in two ISA World Junior Surfing Championships. That competitive background shaped how I think about progression, technique, and what it actually takes to improve in the water.

Over the past several years I have been coaching in Portugal, Costa Rica, Bali, Sri Lanka, and Brazil — working with surfers from intermediate to advanced levels, designing surf programs from scratch, and leading coaching teams across multiple camps.

My background in freediving and scuba adds another layer to how I coach. Breath control, ocean awareness, and comfort in challenging conditions are things I integrate naturally — because they have been part of my own training for years.

ISA Surf Coach Level 2
Two ISA World Junior Championships — represented Argentina
Freediving Instructor — Molchanovs Wave 2
Ocean Rescue Lifeguard certified
Coached and operated in 5 countries
